title: Simultaneous common-stage exactness for finite lisse short-complex diagrams
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and write $g_Y$ for geometric Frobenius. Use the classical lisse adic categories of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], the sf raw rationalized and common-stage constructible hearts of [def-weil-constructible-heart, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and the normalized lisse realization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. Let a finite diagram in the sf common-stage lisse heart be given by prescribed finite-stage lisse models and finitely many rational arrows, specified inverses and equations. Include finitely many short complexes $K_{u}\xrightarrow{f}K_{v}\xrightarrow{h}K_{w}$, with $hf=0$, among this data. Suppose each has short exact normalized point-fibre sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*K_u)\xrightarrow{f_{\bar y}}\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*K_v)\xrightarrow{h_{\bar y}}\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*K_w)\longrightarrow0$$
for every $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$. Then these are short exact sequences in the sf common-stage constructible heart, and all the given data have simultaneous representatives over one finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$ such that each displayed short complex is short exact in the sf finite-stage heart. The objects at this stage may be taken to be scalar extensions of their prescribed lisse models; the arrows, inverse identities and all prescribed equations hold there. Under the finite-stage sf/PBC comparison of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], these sequences are short exact also in the PBC finite-stage heart. Every further finite coefficient extension preserves these assertions. If the diagram carries Weil maps and their inverses, with the Weil-equivariance equations for its arrows included among the prescribed equations, the resulting sequences consist of Weil-equivariant maps with those same realized Weil structures. No exactness of any chosen integral lattice sequence is assumed. Zero short complexes and an empty family of complexes are allowed.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, Lemma 6.8.7 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); faithful extension on normalized fibre complexes and finite common-stage diagrams. Agent refinement for blueprint real-mixed-by-curves paragraph 1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact] to each given short complex in the sf constructible heart. Its geometric datum is exactly $Y_0/k_0$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ as here, and its fibres are the derived point pullback followed by the normalized point-fibre functor, exactly those in the hypothesis. Thus every displayed complex is short exact in the common-stage heart. This uses constructible coefficient fibres, not conservativity of points on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, Lemma 6.8.7 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); normalized constructible-fibre detection as packaged by the cited node

proof.text: For each of these finitely many short exact sequences choose its connecting map $\delta:K_w\to K_u[1]$ by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4). The resulting triangle is distinguished. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], choose a finite-stage distinguished triangle $A\xrightarrow a B\xrightarrow b C\xrightarrow c A[1]$ and an isomorphism from its image to that triangle. Write its components as $\alpha_1:A\simeq K_u$, $\alpha_2:B\simeq K_v$, $\alpha_3:C\simeq K_w$. Include the three inverses and equations $\alpha_2a=f\alpha_1$, $\alpha_3b=h\alpha_2$, $\alpha_1[1]c=\delta\alpha_3$ in the auxiliary finite data.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.6 and admissible heart exact sequences; agent finite-stage assembly using the displayed Hom-colimit definition

proof.text: Keep the prescribed vertex models $M_i$ over their given fields $E_i$. In the Hom colimit of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], choose representatives of every original arrow and inverse, every $\delta$, and all the $\alpha_j^{\pm1}$ just chosen. Take a common finite upper field of their fields, the $E_i$, and the auxiliary triangle fields. Each original equation, inverse identity and triangle square holds as a colimit equality, hence holds over some further finite field. There are finitely many such equalities; take a common upper field $E$ of their witnesses. At this stage keep the vertex objects literally $M_i\otimes_{E_i}E$; no new vertex models are substituted. All auxiliary objects and maps are extended to $E$ with the specified scalar associators and shift comparisons. If pullbacks by $g_Y$ occur, their representatives are the finite-stage pullbacks conjugated by scalar comparisons, as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] identifies these with the prescribed lisse pullbacks and preserves their equations. Thus these are equations between finitely many ordinary arrows at common stages; no injectivity of Hom transition maps is assumed.

source.place: Hom colimit and common-stage composition; the scalar-compatible lisse pullback normalization is the cited realization statement

proof.text: Extend each auxiliary distinguished triangle to $E$ by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated]. The descended inverse identities make the $\alpha_j$ isomorphisms there. Its descended three squares identify it with the triangle on the prescribed objects and arrows $K_{u,E}\xrightarrow{f_E}K_{v,E}\xrightarrow{h_E}K_{w,E}\xrightarrow{\delta_E}K_{u,E}[1]$. This triangle is distinguished by TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The objects $K_{i,E}=M_i\otimes_{E_i}E$ remain in the heart because the standard truncations commute with scalar extension by [prop-constructible-truncations]; they remain lisse by the scalar-compatible equivalence [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. Now [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4) proves short exactness of each $f_E,h_E$ in the sf finite-stage heart.

source.place: Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category, TR1; heart exactness is BBD Theorem 1.3.6 via the cited heart-triangle lemma

proof.text: The comparison $J_{Y,E}$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] is the identity on the common integral category and sends $u\otimes e$ to $u\otimes e$. Consequently it preserves both standard halves: the integral halves are defined by vanishing of the ambient cohomology sheaves, by [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] and [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure], and these are the same sheaves because [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies the two integral categories as one full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_Y))$ with the same completed ring sheaf $A_Y=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ ($Y$ is noetherian, finite-dimensional and $\ell$ is invertible on it); the rational halves are their isomorphism closures, by that definition and [prop-weil-localized-tstructure]. This verifies t-exactness of $J$ and its inverse directly from the definitions. Apply its distinguished-triangle preservation to the triangles in step 4. Their terms lie in the PBC heart, so [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4) makes the same sequences short exact there. We use both the identity formula and the half definitions, not merely an unqualified triangulated equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); agent verification from the common integral identity and the two localized standard-half definitions

proof.text: For any further finite $L/E$, scalar extension preserves the triangles by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated], and preserves the heart by [prop-constructible-truncations]. Hence [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4) again gives short exactness. Functoriality preserves every inverse identity and prescribed equation. The lisse scalar identifications are compatible with towers by [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. The scalar-compatible comparison of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] carries these same assertions to PBC. All maps and triangle witnesses used were rational; no exactness or map stability of a chosen integral lattice sequence was required.

source.place: Exact transitions and finite-stage distinguished triangles; BBD Theorem 1.3.6 for the induced short exact heart sequences

proof.text: When Weil structures are supplied, step 3 includes $\theta_i$, $\theta_i^{-1}$, their inverse equations, and $f\theta_u=\theta_v Lg_Y^*f$, $h\theta_v=\theta_w Lg_Y^*h$. By [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] these equations say exactly that the descended maps are Weil-equivariant; their common-stage classes are the original structures. The normalization in [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] preserves their realized Weil maps. For a zero complex the same construction uses its zero triangle. For an empty family of complexes there are no auxiliary triangles or squares, and step 3 alone descends the diagram; for an empty diagram take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Nothing requires a geometric point when $Y$ is empty.

source.place: Finite representatives, inverse identities and equality witnesses; Weil-pair intertwining is the cited definition

proof_origin.place: Corollary 6.8.5, Lemma 6.8.7 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), with the existing normalized fibre theorem, BBD heart-triangle criterion, and an explicit finite Hom-colimit/triangle-witness assembly. The simultaneous exact descent is an agent argument.
